back: An increase in the proportion of a country's population living in urban areas.
Urban growth is a rise in the number of urban people or built-up area; urbanisation is a rise in the urban share.
Suburbanisation: movement from the centre to the city edge. Sprawl: uncontrolled low-density spread over rural land.
Counter-urbanisation: movement out of large urban areas to smaller settlements. Re-urbanisation: return of people and investment to inner cities.

front: When did the world become more than half urban?
back: In 2007 (United Nations); about two-thirds is projected by 2050.
